summary: Freed space (intro, §1 example, type list, checklist). Added: but-91 for 虽然…但; 以X为目的 as identity-91 with the noun; topic-list :example with 等 as last op; parenthetical clauses as and-conjuncts; consecutive for sequence adverbs, no node for 就/便; mandatory :quote, speaker as ARG0, saying-verb modal full-affirmative, hedged-copula complements author-affirmative; one-time claims performance; aspectual verbs with agent roles share the subject, their nominal objects are process; symmetric 与 → and subject; spouse titles have-rel-role-91; own-noun repeats get a node plus coref; no coref for generic kinds; individual-person for any named being, planet; head+modifier compound split; 其中 as ARG5 in superlatives; implicit-argument for headless superlatives; whole-token lookup for V是; frequency adverbs.

edits.old:
**Make the annotation as correct as you can.** It is compared, node by node and relation by relation,
with an expert gold annotation made by these guidelines, so every concept, sense, role, attribute value
and document-level relation counts. Take the time this needs:

- Read the guidelines below first and look up every decision you are unsure of; annotate a construction an example shows the way the example does.
- Before you go on to the next sentence, check the graph against the guidelines once more: every word
  that carries meaning has its concept, every event its aspect, every role the right direction; and at
  the end check that the document-level relations cover every event and entity the guidelines ask for.
edits.new: **Make the annotation as correct as you can**: it is compared node by node and relation by relation with an expert gold annotation. Read the guidelines first, follow their examples, and check each graph (concepts, aspect, role direction) and the document-level relations before going on.

every later mention, also inside a relative clause, is a re-entrancy.
edits.new: every later pronoun or unexpressed mention, also inside a relative clause, is a re-entrancy (a repeat with its own noun: see 5.3).

edits.old: - a partitive like 其中 (*among them*) is `:mod` on the noun;
edits.new:
- a partitive like 其中 (*among them*) is `:mod` on the noun, but in a superlative it is the `:ARG5` comparison set;
- frequency adverbs (重复, 反复, 经常) are `:frequency`;

Types as in AMR (`country`, `city`, `organization`, `company`, ...). A celestial body is `planet`/`star` + `:name`. Any named being, also a fictional character or alien, is `individual-person`; a descriptor word written as part of the name is an `:op`.

edits.old: Use `:ARG5` only for an explicit comparison set
edits.new: A superlative with no head noun (最大 + classifier) is `(i / implicit-argument :unit <classifier> :ARG1-of (h / have-degree-91 ...))`. Use `:ARG5` only for an explicit comparison set

edits.old: 1. Look it up as the whole segmented token. A two-character verb is not cut down to its first character.
edits.new: 1. Look it up as the whole segmented token. A two-character verb (also a V是 token like 算是) is not cut down to its first character.

*although* (虽然, 尽管) → `:concession` only when the main clause has no adversative word; when it is answered by 但/但是/不过/却, use `(b / but-91 :ARG1 concessive :ARG2 main)` (a further clause added to the concessive part makes `:ARG1` an `and`).
- A sequence adverb linking two clauses (后来, 然后, 接着) → `(c / consecutive :op1 first :op2 later)` (or `after`/`before`); the adverb and an additive 还 with it get no node. Focus particles 就, 便 get no node.
- A clause in parentheses restating or exemplifying the previous one is a conjunct under `and`.
- 以 X 为 目的/目标/宗旨 is copular: keep the noun, `(i / identity-91 :ARG1 (m / 目的 :purpose-of E) :ARG2 X :aspect state)`; a quantifier (大部分) is `:mod` on E.
- N 有 A、B…等 where N is a topic, content or category noun listing its members: no 有/`have-91` node; N fills its outer role and takes `:example (a / and :op1 A ... :opk 等)`. 等 / *etc.* closing a list is always its last `:opN`, not `:mod`.

edits.old: A true idiom stays one concept.
edits.new: A true idiom stays one concept. A compound of a free head noun + modifier (母公司 type) is split: `head :mod modifier`.

edits.old: It is not an argument of the aspectual verb as well. Check the aspectual verb's roleset.
edits.new:
This holds only when the aspectual verb's roleset has no agent role. If it has one (继续, 停止 with an `:ARG0` agent), in any clause the subject fills that role and is re-entered as the agent of the governed verb or event nominal (停止 X 的 V: the stopper is V's agent too).
- **Symmetric predicates.** A 与/和/跟 B + symmetric predicate (have a relation, meet, marry): `(a / and :op1 A :op2 B)` fills the subject role; B is not `:companion`.

edits.old: In Chinese documents write the role predicates as `have-org-role-91` / `have-rel-role-91`.
edits.new: In Chinese documents write the role predicates as `have-org-role-91` / `have-rel-role-91`; spouse and kin titles (夫人, wife) use `have-rel-role-91`, and a modifying country is `:place` on the role noun.

edits.old:
Reported speech and thought: the reported event is the `:ARG1` of the reporting verb, as in AMR. The
UMR release data also marks it with `:quote <reporting event>` when the content is a quotation.
edits.new: Reported speech and thought: the reported event is the `:ARG1` of the reporting verb, as in AMR, and every content clause of a verb of saying, claiming, alleging or sloganeering also gets `:quote <that verb>`, quoted or not. The speaker fills the saying verb's `:ARG0` (a periodical too); do not re-enter it into the content unless the text makes it its subject. For passives like 被指 choose the claim / point-out sense.

edits.old: - **Repeated activity of an institution or periodical** (publishing, broadcasting, reporting, what it regularly contains or covers) is `habitual`, even with 了 or other completion marking.
edits.new: - **Repeated activity of an institution or periodical** (publishing, broadcasting, reporting, what it regularly contains or covers) is `habitual`, even with 了 or other completion marking. A one-time claim or statement is `performance`; an event nominal object of an aspectual verb is `process`.

edits.new: node, or an event used as conceiver). Saying and claiming verbs are not modal predicates: their content is `full-affirmative` from the speaker (or the conceiver the clause names), never `unspecified`. An event inside a hedged copula's complement keeps `(author :full-affirmative e)`.

edits.old: - Within one sentence, coreference is a re-entrancy in the graph (one variable), not a `:coref` triple.
edits.new:
- Within one sentence, a pronoun or unexpressed repeat is a re-entrancy; a mention written out again with its own noun (a shortened name, a common noun) gets its own node and a `:coref` triple.
- Do not link generic or kind-level mentions of a class (bare nouns in a topic list, generic subjects).

edits.old:
- Parentheses balanced; every variable defined once; all variables start with `s<N>`.
- Every event has `:aspect` (`have-degree-91` excepted); negated events have `:polarity -` (fused negation verbs excepted).
- Every Chinese predicate uses the sense and numbered roles of its own PropBank roleset (`:ARG1` only if the roleset has one).
- Before writing `:coref`, drop every pair where both mentions are only `:place`/`:mod` modifiers.
- Every event and time expression has a temporal parent; every event has a modal parent.
- Coreference across sentences is in `:coref`; within a sentence it is a re-entrancy.
edits.new:
- Balanced parentheses; each variable defined once, starting with `s<N>`.
- Every event has `:aspect`, a temporal and a modal parent (exceptions above); Chinese predicates use their own roleset's sense and roles.
- No `:coref` pair of two mere `:place`/`:mod` modifiers or generic mentions.
